newsitem.title: UK: Stress can be deadly for HIV victims - report.
newsitem.headline: Stress can be deadly for HIV victims - report.

text.p: Intense psychological stress such as the death of a loved one could be deadly to people with HIV, the virus that leads to AIDS, Britain's New Scientist magazine reported on Thursday.
Researchers in the United States found that a single episode of stress, if it is sufficiently harrowing, can double the rate at which HIV-positive men develop the symptoms of AIDS.
Robert Golden, a psychiatrist at the University of North Carolina School of Medicine, and colleagues studied 93 men with HIV who had not yet showed symptoms of AIDS.
Thirty-five of the men developed AIDS symptoms over nearly four years.

The men who had experienced one or more episodes of severe stress, such as the death of someone close or the break-up of a long-term relationship, were twice as likely to develop further symptoms as those for whom life had gone more smoothly.
